column1: # *** THE SAN JOSE LERENA ARE OURS, AND THIS ARCHIVE SAID THEY WERE NOT. ***
# 21 September 2026. On 14 September a row here tested ZELMIRA CARLOTA LERENA LARRIERA, born
# 4 November 1880 in the Departamento de San Jose, and concluded: 'TESTED AND PLACED - and she
# is NOT ours.' It then named the one thing that might change that - her father ALBERTO LERENA,
# fathering a daughter in 1880 - and wrote: 'NOTHING JOINS THEM but a forename and an age,
# which is precisely the evidence that produced the two Arturos.'
# *** SOMETHING JOINS THEM NOW, AND IT IS THE OTHER GRANDFATHER. ***
# The row's candidate was ALBERTO OCTAVIO LERENA LENGUAS, born 22 March 1850, son of Luis and
# Justiniana. *** It is not him. *** Alberto Lerena's own Montevideo death registration of
# 2 March 1921 names his wife MARIA INES LARRIERA and his parents AVELINO LERENA and AMBROSIA
# TREIBEL - so Zelmira's father is PEDRO ALBERTO YSABELINO LERENA TRAIBEL, born at the Aguada
# on 16 March 1852, and Zelmira is a great-granddaughter of Sancho after all.

column1: *** MARIA INES LERENA LARRIERA (de GARDONE) ***
# ================= 1. THE CHAIN, WRITTEN OUT SO IT CAN BE ATTACKED =================
#   Zelmira Carlota, b. San Jose 4 Nov 1880       -- her birth and baptism name her parents
#     father ALBERTO LERENA, mother MARIA INES LARRIERA
#   Alberto Lerena, d. Montevideo 1 Mar 1921      -- certificate 246, ark 1:1:6LD5-X4PR
#     wife MARIA INES LARRIERA; father AVELINO LERENA; mother AMBROSIA TREIBEL
#   Avelino Lerena, d. 22 Aug 1890                -- 1858 and 1852 parish acts
#     father SANCHO LERENA; mother MARIA FERNANDEZ
# *** THE WEAK LINK WAS THE MIDDLE ONE. IT WAS OPENED THE SAME DAY - SEE SECTION 4. *** It had
# been read at INDEX LEVEL ONLY; the image has not been opened. Everything rests on one record
# that happens to name both the wife and both parents in the same entry - which is exactly what
# makes it strong, and exactly why it should be seen. *** ERRAND: open Montevideo civil death
# registration No. 246 of 2 March 1921. ***
# The alternative would be two men called Alberto Lerena each married to a woman called Maria
# Ines Larriera. That is not a serious reading, and it is written down so that nobody has to
# wonder whether it was considered.
# ================ 2. AND THE NAMES ARE THE CORROBORATION, NOT THE PROOF ================
# Alberto and Maria Ines named their children *** MARIA ADELINA *** - his sister, born 1865 -
# *** CARLOS AMBROSIO *** - his brother on the family chart, who stood godfather to that same
# sister in 1865 - and *** ANGEL MIGUEL AVELINO ***, for his father. Three of eight children
# carry names out of the household at the Aguada. *** That is corroboration and it is not
# evidence: *** these are common names, and this archive has been burned by exactly this
# reasoning before. The death registration is the evidence. The names are why one believes it.
# ================== 3. WHAT THIS MOVES, BEYOND ONE WOMAN'S PARENTS ==================
# The register has carried a SAN JOSE DE MAYO cluster since its first fortnight - Echeverry,
# Alejandro Lerena, Barbara Lerena, and Mauricio Lerena who married Casimira Montano there in
# 1837 - all unattached, in a department the Montevideo trunk never reached. *** This is the
# first documented Lerena of the Montevideo trunk living in San Jose ***, from his daughter's
# birth in 1879 to his son's in 1898. It does not join the San Jose cluster to anything. It
# puts a known man in the room where that cluster lives, which is a different and smaller thing
# - and a reason to look again at the four departments.
# ============== 4. THE ERRAND WAS DONE BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN DOWN ==============
# Act No. 246, Montevideo, 2 March 1921 - *** film 008165205 image 01604, IMAGE READ 21 September 2026. ***
# *** 'Que el finado era hijo de AVELINO LERENA, fallecido, y de AMBROSIA TREIBEL, fallecida.' ***
# So the chain rests on an image at every step that matters, and the act adds four things the
# index never carried:
#   HE WAS BORN AT MONTEVIDEO - 'de nacionalidad oriental, NACIDO EN MONTEVIDEO' - which is where
#   Pedro Alberto Ysabelino was baptised, and NOT where his own nine children were born.
#   HE WAS A RENTISTA, and died 'a consecuencia de CARCINOMA DE LA VEJIGA, segun consta del
#   certificado del Dr. LUSSICH', at six in the morning, at the calle JUAN PAULLIER.
#   THE DECLARANTS WERE NOT FAMILY - Juan Miramonte, fifty, of 18 de Julio, and Pedro Fernandez,
#   forty-eight, of Cerrito 230. *** Which is why his age is wrong by fifteen days: *** two
#   neighbours said sixty-nine of a man who would have turned sixty-nine on 16 March.
#   *** AND IT COUNTS THE CHILDREN, WHICH IS THE FIND: 'de cuya union quedan NUEVE HIJOS llamados:
#   Maria Adelina, Zelmira, ELEIZA, Alberto, Carlos, Maria Ines, Maria Consuelo, Maria Antonieta y
#   Miguel Avelino.' ***
# Eight of those nine are the eight the parent-pair query found. *** The third is a daughter no
# index here has matched, and her name is not securely read - ELEIZA or ELOIZA. *** She was read
# at three times magnification and the archive still cannot choose. She is entered as a person,
# with the uncertainty in her name, because a child named on her father's death act exists whether
# or not a birth registration has been located for her.
# *** AND THE ACT IS A BETTER WITNESS THAN NINE INDEX ENTRIES WOULD BE. *** The eight children were
# found by asking an index for records that name two parents - eight separate entries, which look
# like eight independent confirmations and are one indexing project. This single act, written from
# the declarations of two men who knew the household, is a different occasion and a different
# mouth. It confirms the eight and corrects the count.
